title: How does a write reach the disk?
question: A write goes to memory first. What does fsync() do to make it durable?

stops.note: Into the page cache: the page is dirty, and no block is chosen for it yet (delayed allocation). Nothing is on the disk.
Now the data must reach the disk.
Write the dirty page back: the multiblock allocator picks it a block, from the block bitmap.
The journal (jbd2, its own thread) commits the metadata changes: the bitmaps, the inode, the directory block.
The block layer: an I/O request to the disk, /dev/loop0, whose blocks are a file in memory.
